method: Personally expanded transparent arithmetic and limits from the assigned source; not a literature reread.

W.3.shape: 2*3=6; reshaping to 6 or back to 2x3 preserves order for this contiguous input; 8 elements cannot hold the same six values.

W.4.probabilities: Three cat cards and one dog card, each equally likely: p(cat)=3/4, p(dog)=1/4, sum=1. Mutually exclusive exhaustive cat/dog probabilities .9+.9=1.8 violate normalization.
W.4.log: For p=e^a>0, ln(p)=a. For 0<p<1, a<0, hence -ln(p)>0; -ln(1)=0. d[-ln(p)]/dp=-1/p<0, so smaller positive p has higher cost. As p→0+, -ln(p)→+∞; ln(0) has no finite real value.
W.4.product: For positive p1,p2, ln(p1*p2)=ln(p1)+ln(p2). If two correctness events are independent with probabilities .5,.5, their joint probability is .25 and negative log cost is 2*ln(2)=1.386294361. Independence is the required condition for this particular product of marginal probabilities; the log identity itself only needs positive factors.

W.5.shape: C_ij=sum_{k=0}^2 A_ik B_kj. Each fixed i remains a distinct recipe; 2x3 @ 3x2 → 2x2.
W.5.bias: Adding bias [5,0] gives [[45,1],[85,6]]. Bias [8,0] gives [[48,1],[88,6]], a cost-only +3 per row.

W.6.derivative: For L(w)=(w-3)^2, [L(w+h)-L(w)]/h=2(w-3)+h. Limit gives 2(w-3), equal to -4 at 1 and -3.2 at 1.4.
W.6.limitation: These are exact real-number calculations for this scalar quadratic. The float32 probe allows 1e-6 for w and 2e-6 for loss. Negative local derivative alone is not a finite-step improvement guarantee.

W.2_bits: 3=0b11; 3<<4=0b110000=48; OR with 5=0b000101 gives 0b110101=53. Right-shift four bits returns 3; AND 0b1111 returns 5.
